content:
Apple is reportedly taking a new approach to bringing artificial intelligence features to users in China: training its own large language model with the assistance of Alibaba.

Reuters reported that three sources described this China-exclusive model as a major shift in Apple's strategy away from relying on third-party models.

Alibaba is reportedly providing support for the model's training, though neither party has commented.

Models such as ChatGPT and Claude are currently unavailable in mainland China, making Apple's local strategy temporarily different from that in other major markets.

This development comes ahead of Alibaba confirming its partnership with Apple in February 2025; earlier, Chinese internet regulators had also completed the registration for Apple Intelligence to enable its use on iPhones.

Previous reports indicated that Alibaba's Qwen model and Baidu's technology would be incorporated into the localised system.

Reuters noted that it remains unclear how Apple's new model will work with other third-party models. The report said Apple Intelligence is expected to launch in China within the coming months following an iOS update.

Meanwhile, Apple's significantly revamped Siri AI will be publicly released this autumn with iOS 27, but only in regions where it has been made available.

Initial support will be limited to specified English-language versions, with the rollout for iPhone and iPad in the European Union delayed. The launch timeline for China has yet to be determined.
